correctness.rationale: PASS. On the unit cube boundary with fixed origin vertex, incident-face intrinsic distance is √(u²+v²); opposite face x=1 has squared distance 1+u²+v²+2min(u,v). The candidate is globally 1-Lipschitz under face gluing and realized by feasible unfolded paths, so is the true intrinsic shortest distance. Splitting opposite-face square by u<v maps uniform radial areas to right triangle T={(1,0),(1,1),(2,1)}. Hence F(r)=1/2 area([0,1]²∩B_r)+area(T∩B_r), whose polar integration gives the three Φ_c branches and density. Uniform coordinate moments yield E[D²]=(2/3+7/3)/2=3/2. Direct one-sided differentiations give jumps −1 at 1 and √2 and +5/6 at √5; a local wedge calculation gives tail (5/12)ε². Independent square/triangle grid checked multiple thresholds; analytical face metric and integration establish all r.
